parsed.explanation: Thin, trans-silent dossier; extrapolation is required and must lean on structural signals. The one hard fact is an unenforced 14-year same-sex-conduct statute — per the rubric a secondary, dead-letter factor (no prosecutions in 2010–2013 foreign reporting, no documented use as a police lever against gender-nonconforming people). Governance looks rule-of-law-ish: no security-force abuses recorded, functioning courts. Offsetting negatives: repeated elite hostility framing LGBT people via religion and criminal code (social-hostility rhetoric, not state threat-framing of trans people), no non-discrimination protection, no recognition machinery, and rejected reform — climate signals of official disapproval that could license street hostility a visitor has thin recourse against. No trans-specific targeting, facility rules, document practice, or violence data exists in either direction, so the record cannot show safety, only absence of documented harm in a state where institutions otherwise leave records — a modestly positive signal but not proof. This sits a step below a dead-letter-statute-plus-documented-acceptance jurisdiction (0.65-C tier): same statute profile, but here no documented acceptance of gender diversity and active elite condemnation. Above 0.55 targets only where a recurring visitor-facing harm is documented — none is. 0.58.
